display.purpose: The start page's single h1 only.

headline.purpose: Page heads, the palette input, an elicitation message.

title.purpose: Tool and resource titles (700), server name, card h3, selected method, brand word.

body.purpose: Descriptions, parameter tables, form labels; buttons, nav and tree rows run at 12.5px.

body-small.purpose: Sub-lines, types, notes, status bar, detail and pair heads, tabs.

protocol.purpose: Everything the protocol says: stream rows, filter, ids, latencies, JSON, readouts, key legends.

label.purpose: h4 section labels, tree group heads, stream column headers, palette groups, message roles. Names the block beneath; never a kicker above a title.

tag.purpose: Kind tags (TOOL / REQ / RES), status pills, kbd legends, row actions.

shadows.name: drawer
shadows.purpose: The rail when it is a drawer below 1100px.

shadows.name: pill
shadows.purpose: The amber jump-to-latest capsule floating over the stream.

shadows.name: led-halo
shadows.purpose: The connected LED's soft ring; a glow, not a lift.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Background and border transitions on buttons, chips, resizers, the display filter.

motion.name: landed
motion.purpose: A frame entering the stream flashes from Amber Select to Amber Soft and holds the tint until acknowledged.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion removes every animation and transition; the LED stays at full opacity; the held tint remains.

breakpoints.name: rail-drawer
breakpoints.purpose: Below this the rail is a drawer over the work area.

breakpoints.name: bar-compact
breakpoints.purpose: Capture bar keeps the active chip, drops button labels to icons, hides status-bar key legends.

breakpoints.name: stream-no-id
breakpoints.purpose: Stream drops id and latency (Δ) columns.

breakpoints.name: pair-stack
breakpoints.purpose: Detail pane stacks the request/response pair.

breakpoints.name: crafter-no-hint
breakpoints.purpose: Crafter hides the send shortcut hint.

narrative.overview:
mcptool borrows Wireshark's grammar and nothing of its skin. The live JSON-RPC stream is the main pane; every other surface (the tree of offerings on the left, the dissected frame below, the crafter on the right) is a way of composing or taking apart a frame in that stream. The world is a cool graphite neutral scale, dark first with a light sibling that follows the OS preference, drawn with hairline rules, dense 24px rows, tabular figures and LED status dots. Nothing is decorative; a line exists because two things need separating, and a tint exists because a frame has a direction.

Colour is a budget, not a palette. One amber is spent on exactly four things: the selection, the primary action, the focus ring, and a change held until it is seen. Two direction hues (blue for client to server, green for server to client) and one error red are the only other chroma on screen, and they appear only where direction or failure is the fact being shown. JSON, JWT parts and readouts rank by weight and ink level, never by hue.

Type is Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for the interface and Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono for everything the protocol says (methods, ids, latencies, JSON, the display filter, key legends). Inside any one pane there are two sizes; hierarchy is weight and case. The rejected arrangement is the category's own: document tabs over a request/response split with the log folded away at the bottom.
keyCharacteristics: Stream-first three-column workbench under a 44px capture bar and over a 26px mono status bar.
Flat tonal layering on four graphite steps; hairlines at 8% and 15% white (10% and 20% near-black in light).
Amber budget: selection, primary action, focus, held-until-seen. Blue out, green in, red error. Nothing else coloured.
Two sizes per pane (13 / 11.5; protocol mono 12); rank by weight (400 / 500 / 600 / 700) and uppercase.
One drawn inline-SVG icon set on a 16-unit grid at stroke 1.75, always currentColor.
Motion is 150 to 200ms and state-bound; a landed frame flashes once and holds its tint until acknowledged.

rules.name: The Amber Budget Rule
rules.body: Amber is spent on four things only: the selected frame, the primary action, the focus ring, and a change held until it is seen. If a surface needs a fifth, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Direction-Only Rule
rules.body: Blue and green mean client to server and server to client and appear only on direction marks, kind tags, row tints and REQ/RES tags. They never colour a button, a heading, a link or a JSON token.

rules.name: The Rank-By-Weight Rule
rules.body: JSON keys, numbers and booleans are Ink at 600; strings are Ink 2; null and punctuation are Ink 3. The JWT's header, payload and signature are 700 Ink, 400 Ink 2, 400 Ink 3. No syntax hue anywhere.

rules.name: The Two-Size Rule
rules.body: Inside one pane there are two type sizes (13 and 11.5, or mono 12 and 11.5). Anything that needs to stand out does so by weight or by uppercase, not by a third size.

rules.name: The Protocol Speaks Mono Rule
rules.body: Method names, ids, latencies, JSON, filter syntax, counts in readouts and key legends are set in Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono. The interface's own words stay in the sans.

rules.name: The Flat Work Rule
rules.body: Nothing inside the work area casts a shadow. Only what floats over it (dialog, palette, drawer, jump pill) does.

dos: Do spend amber only on the selection, the primary action, the focus ring and a change held until seen (The Amber Budget Rule).
Do use blue for client to server and green for server to client, and only on direction marks, kind tags, row tints and REQ/RES tags.
Do set everything the protocol says (methods, ids, latencies, JSON, filter syntax, key legends) in Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono at 12px with tabular figures.
Do keep two type sizes per pane and rank by weight (400 / 500 / 600 / 700) and uppercase.
Do rank JSON and JWT parts by weight and ink level (Ink 600, Ink 2, Ink 3), never by hue.
Do separate with 1px hairlines (Line for dividers, Line Strong for controls) and raise with tone (Graphite 0 → 1 → 2 → 3).
Do show counts as one mono readout line: quiet label, heavy value.
Do hold an unacknowledged frame in Amber Soft with no timer; it cools only when seen.
Do draw every icon from the one inline-SVG set (16-unit grid, stroke 1.75, currentColor).
Do use --accent-text for amber as text so the light theme gets its darker amber.
donts: Don't add kickers or eyebrows above a title; a Label-style h4 names the block beneath it and nothing else.
Don't build hero-metric tiles; counts belong on the readout line.
Don't put a border on side tabs or frame an unseen frame; a background tint holds it.
Don't use Unicode glyphs (arrows, bullets, check marks) as icons.
Don't cast a shadow inside the work area; only dialogs, the palette, the drawer and the jump pill float.
Don't colour a button, heading, link or JSON token with blue or green.
Don't introduce a third type size inside a pane or a system display face.
Don't let any text fall below 4.5:1 in either theme; Ink 3 is the floor.
